correctness.rationale: The proof identifies the group algebra as a direct sum of central polynomial modules indexed by a symplectic quotient. The strong identity L_n[v]=I_S I^(n-2) is proved both inclusions by an induction with explicit nonorthogonal witnesses. Squarefree monomial counting yields the claimed formula for every r and characteristic-two field; tensoring with finite abelian factors multiplies dimensions by |A|. Independent table-level binary computations for D8, Q8, mixed products in ranks 1–2 and central polynomial recursion in rank 3 match exactly. Limits (raw subspaces, char2, direct products) are explicit.

evidence: Bhandari–Passi, Bull. London Math. Soc. 24 (1992), pp. 68–70, studies lower/upper indices and defines lower Lie powers as two-sided ideals generated by nested commutators.
GAP LAGUNA manual section 4.5-20 likewise defines the lower Lie powers as associative ideals.
For D8 in characteristic two the raw second product subspace has dimension 3, while the two-sided ideal it generates has dimension 4; therefore their dimension spectra are not interchangeable.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The published index classifications include the special case of the nilpotency index r+2 in parts of their ranges, and this is not claimed as a previously unknown index. They do not by implication determine the stronger exact sizes of the unclosed Lie subspaces, whose inequivalence to the standard associative-ideal filtration is visible already at r=1.

value.rationale: The work determines every level and every central quotient component of a natural group-ring Lie/Jordan filtration for an all-rank noncommutative family; only the nilpotency index was previously available from the closest sources. The top nonzero layer has dimension |A|(4^r-1) rather than the full central ideal rank, and the identical spectrum for any dihedral/quaternion mixture reveals an invariant blind to those different group structures. This is a complete structural invariant, not an arbitrary small numerical example.
